newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds end almost unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds end almost unchanged.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds closed almost unchanged on Tuesday despite heavy selling by the mutual funds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.01 pct to 173.05
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 pct to 163.27.
Volume was high at 271 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams.
On Monday there was no trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange due to a general strike by the Histadrut trade union federation.

On Wednesday trading is suspended to enable the exchange to alter the system for pricing bonds, introduce new indices and rewind the rest to 100 points. The change is technical and will not cause a change in the actual value of the bonds.

"Trading was very active today because there was no trading on Monday. The big mutual funds, which specialize in unlinked bonds, sold bonds heavily to gain tax benefits before the end of the month," said Yoram Ben-Yaeir of Ahrayut Investment Management.

Inflation-linked bonds rose, reflecting the continued positive trend in long bonds. "Despite the rise the market is stable and is expected to remain at the current level," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
Unlinked bonds closed almost unchanged despite selling by the mutual funds. "The market is very balanced. I believe it will remain sleepy at the beginning of the new year," Ben-Yaeir said.
Makams were stable, but volume swelled to 100 million shekels.

Traders said dollar-linked bonds closed lower following the rise of the shekel against the dollar. On Tuesday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2510 shekels against 3.2610 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
